A linear equation in one variable can be written in the form ax + b = 0, where a and b are constants and a is not zero. Solving such an equation means finding the value of x that makes the statement true. The basic strategy is to isolate the variable on one side of the equals sign. You may add or subtract the same quantity from both sides without changing the solution. You may also multiply or divide both sides by any nonzero number. Each of these operations produces an equivalent equation, one with exactly the same solution set. When the variable appears on both sides, collect like terms first. Always check your answer by substituting it back into the original equation.
